column1: # Production and security findings the dev-setup change deliberately leaves
# alone - out of its dev-only scope - with where each one is, what it costs and
# the follow-up. Suite A (test/lib/SuiteStatic.ps1) re-checks every row on
# every run and reports it as INFO R-PROD-<id>: "<location>: <impact>
# file   paths relative to the homecrew root (the directory holding the fifteen
#        checkouts); * and ? are wildcards within one path segment. Several
#        specs are separated by ;; and must ALL hold for the finding to count
#        as present; one spec with a wildcard holds when ANY file matches.
# regex  a .NET regular expression, one per file spec (separated by ;;) or one
#        for all of them, matched against the whole file with Multiline on
#        (^ and $ are line anchors) and CRLF read as LF. It must match while
#        the finding exists, so a finding about something MISSING is written
#        as a negative lookahead over the whole file: (?s)\A(?!.*<fix>).*<anchor>.
# Tab-separated, one row per finding, ASCII only.

column3: Production publishes 5432, 9092, 8761, 8888, 8080-8089 and 4200 on all interfaces, and Docker's own iptables rules bypass ufw, so postgres, kafka, eureka and config-server are reachable from outside unless the provider's firewall stops them.
column4: Bind the internal ports to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml, or drop them, keeping only what the reverse proxy needs; or filter in the DOCKER-USER chain on the host.

column3: The broker listens and advertises PLAINTEXT with no authentication, and 9092 is published on every interface (R-PROD-01): whoever reaches the host can produce to and consume from every topic.
column4: Stop publishing 9092 in production; if an outside client ever needs Kafka, add a SASL_SSL listener for it.

column3: The deploy copies only docker-compose.yml to /opt/homecrew, but postgres mounts ./postgres/init from next to it; on the host that directory does not exist, so a fresh postgres volume never gets the per-service databases.
column4: Copy postgres/init in the deploy (or bake the SQL into an image), and fail the deploy when it is missing.

column3: The healthcheck always probes user and database homecrew, whatever POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_DB say: with other values postgres logs a FATAL for every probe, and the check never looks at the database the services use.
column4: Probe with pg_isready -U "$${POSTGRES_USER}" -d "$${POSTGRES_DB}" instead of the literal names.

column3: Every production service runs a mutable :dev tag, so a deploy or a restart after a pull runs whatever was pushed last, and a rollback has no fixed image to go back to.
column4: Tag images with the commit SHA (or pin them by digest) and have deploy.yml set the tag explicitly.

column3: The runner trusts whatever host key answers for HETZNER_HOST at deploy time - trust on first use, on every run - so a spoofed host would be accepted and handed everything the deploy sends, the .env secrets included.
column4: Keep the host's public key in a secret (for example HETZNER_KNOWN_HOSTS) and write that to known_hosts instead of scanning for it.

column2: home-crew-*/Dockerfile (the twelve service images: no USER instruction)
column3: The production JVMs run as root inside their containers, so a remote code execution in any service is root in that container, with every capability Docker grants by default.
column4: Add a non-root USER to the service Dockerfile template in _standards and roll it out to the twelve repositories.

column3: The Maven distribution the wrapper downloads is not checksummed, so a tampered download would be run as it is - in CI, on developer machines and in every dev container.
column4: Add distributionSha256Sum for apache-maven-3.9.16-bin.zip to the _standards template and roll it out.

column3: The production image copies only package.json and runs npm install, so every build resolves dependency versions afresh instead of using the committed package-lock.json: builds are not reproducible, and a compromised new release goes straight in.
column4: COPY package.json package-lock.json ./ and RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund - the lockfile is committed now, which is the condition the comment there was waiting for.

column3: The comment says home-crew-config is public, while docker-compose.yml, deploy.yml and the README treat it as private (config-server clones it with CONFIG_GIT_TOKEN); whichever is wrong, someone will act on it.
column4: Decide which is true, then fix the comment or the repository's visibility, and keep CONFIG_GIT_TOKEN required only while it is private.

column3: The README and a comment in docker-compose.yml say there is deliberately no homecrew_assignment database, but the init SQL creates homecrew_assignment - and homecrew_notification - for two services that have no datasource.
column4: Either drop the two CREATE DATABASE lines or correct the README and the compose comment.

column3: The dev image downloads the mvnd tarball without verifying a checksum, so a tampered release asset would run in every dev container, next to checkouts that are mounted read-write.
column4: Pin the tarball's sha256 per architecture in Dockerfile.dev and check it with sha256sum -c before extracting.

column2: home-crew-*/Dockerfile* (FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jre, eclipse-temurin:25-jdk, node:24-alpine, nginx:1.29-alpine) and docker-compose.yml (postgres:18, apache/kafka:4.1.0)
column3: Base and infrastructure images are pinned by tag, not by digest, so the same commit can build or run different bytes on different days.
column4: Pin by digest (image@sha256:...) and let a bot such as Renovate or Dependabot move the digests.

column3: Every container comes back whenever Docker starts, the local dev stack included: a laptop that was not stopped with ./dev down restarts twelve JVMs and their compile loops at every Docker Desktop launch.
column4: Consider restart: "no" (or on-failure) for the dev services in compose.dev.yml; production keeps unless-stopped.

column3: .mvn/jvm.config and lombok.config fall under * text=auto, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf gets CRLF; Maven and Lombok tolerate it today, but anything else that reads them line by line may not.
column4: Add .mvn/jvm.config text eol=lf and lombok.config text eol=lf to _standards/templates/gitattributes and re-run apply.py.
